value.title: Fleet manifest schema, loader, and child config builder
value.description: Create the src/fleet/ module with a Zod-validated FleetManifest schema, a FleetManifestLoader.load() that reads and validates a manifest JSON file, and a buildChildConfig() that produces a Zod-valid DeepSeek (openai-compat) BoberConfig per child via createDefaultConfig() plus a shallow override merge. This is the deterministic foundation every later sprint builds on, and it tackles the ADR-2 config-validity risk first.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully (tsc) with zero errors after the change.
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors.
ESLint reports zero errors on all new/modified files (consistent-type-imports, no unused, ESM .js import extensions).

A Zod FleetManifestSchema exists with rootDir (default '.'), concurrency (int >= 1, default 3), and children (non-empty array of {folder, task, config?}); FleetManifestLoader.load(path) reads the file, JSON-parses, and schema-parses it, returning a typed FleetManifest.
load() throws a clear error (naming the failing field/path) when the file is missing (ENOENT), not valid JSON, has an empty children array, or has concurrency < 1.
buildChildConfig(child) returns an object that passes BoberConfigSchema validation and sets the openai-compat/DeepSeek provider on planner, generator, and evaluator sections.

When a child supplies a `config` override, buildChildConfig shallow-merges its top-level keys over the base config (child top-level keys replace base keys), and the merged result still passes BoberConfigSchema.
All existing tests continue to pass with zero failures.

nonGoals: No folder scaffolding, git init, or subprocess spawning (Sprint 2)
No mapBounded fan-out or outcome aggregation (Sprint 3)
No CLI command registration or runFleet entrypoint (Sprint 4)
No deep/recursive config merge — shallow only
stopConditions: All eight success criteria pass programmatic or manual verification
load() round-trips a valid example manifest and buildChildConfig() output validates against BoberConfigSchema for both the no-override and with-override cases
value.definitionOfDone: src/fleet/manifest.ts exports FleetManifestSchema, FleetManifest/ChildSpec types, and a FleetManifestLoader (or load function); src/fleet/child-config.ts (or manifest.ts) exports buildChildConfig(child): BoberConfig built from createDefaultConfig() + DeepSeek overrides + shallow child.config merge. Collocated *.test.ts cover valid load, each invalid-load path, base config validity, and the shallow-merge case. Build, typecheck, and lint are clean and all tests pass.
assumptions: createDefaultConfig() and BoberConfigSchema in src/config/schema.ts are the source of schema-correct defaults and the validation gate (ADR-2).
DeepSeek is wired as the openai-compat provider; the exact provider string/endpoint/providerConfig shape follows src/providers/factory.ts and openai-compat.ts.
Per-child config override is a shallow top-level merge (resolved clarification Q1-config-merge).
outOfScope: Scaffolding, git, subprocess, fan-out, aggregation, reporting, CLI (later sprints)
Validating that DEEPSEEK_API_KEY is set (Sprint 4 fail-fast check)
value.generatorNotes:
Create the new module under src/fleet/.

1. READ FIRST: src/config/schema.ts (createDefaultConfig + BoberConfigSchema, the exact role sections planner/generator/evaluator and their provider/endpoint/providerConfig fields), src/providers/factory.ts (how openai-compat/DeepSeek is dispatched — provider string, endpoint, providerConfig.apiKey, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY env), src/providers/openai-compat.ts, and an existing Zod schema in src/config/schema.ts for the .default()/.optional() conventions.

2. manifest.ts: define FleetChildSchema = z.object({ folder: z.string().min(1), task: z.string().min(1), config: z.record(z.string(), z.unknown()).optional() }) and FleetManifestSchema = z.object({ rootDir: z.string().default('.'), concurrency: z.number().int().min(1).default(3), children: z.array(FleetChildSchema).min(1) }). Export inferred types. load(manifestPath) uses node:fs/promises readFile (async only — no sync fs), JSON.parse, then FleetManifestSchema.parse(); let Zod/JSON errors propagate with a helpful message (wrap to name the manifest path).

3. buildChildConfig(child): start from createDefaultConfig() (pass whatever args it requires — check its signature), then set the DeepSeek/openai-compat provider on planner, generator, and evaluator (mirror exactly how factory.ts expects provider+endpoint+providerConfig). Then shallow-merge child.config: { ...base, ...(child.config ?? {}) } at the TOP level only. Return the object; optionally BoberConfigSchema.parse() it to guarantee validity by construction.

4. Use import type { ... } for type-only imports. ESM: every relative import ends in .js. No `any` — use unknown + narrowing.

5. Collocate manifest.test.ts (and child-config.test.ts if separate). Tests create temp manifest files in a temp dir (node:fs/promises mkdtemp) and clean up — do NOT mock fs (principles).
value.evaluatorNotes:
Independently verify each criterion.
sc-1-4/sc-1-5: Inspect the Zod schema for the exact defaults and constraints; run the unit tests covering valid load + each invalid path (missing file, bad JSON, empty children, concurrency 0/negative). Confirm errors are thrown, not swallowed, and mention the failing field.
sc-1-6: Confirm buildChildConfig output BoberConfigSchema.parse()-es without throwing and that planner/generator/evaluator each carry the openai-compat/DeepSeek provider exactly as factory.ts expects (check the provider string + endpoint + providerConfig shape against src/providers/factory.ts).
sc-1-7: Confirm a child with a `config` override produces a merged config where the overridden top-level key is the child's value and untouched keys retain the base, and the result still validates.
sc-1-8: Run the full test suite; zero failures.
Also check: no synchronous fs calls, all relative imports use .js extensions, import type used for types.

value.title: Child folder scaffolding and subprocess runner
value.description: Implement ChildScaffolder.scaffold() (mkdir + write Zod-valid config + git init, with all failures captured as data and non-empty folders skipped) and ChildRunner.run() (spawn one `agent-bober run` child via execa with reject:false, a default per-child timeout, and CLI-entry resolution via the parent's own dist/cli/index.js). Tackles ADR-4 (entry resolution) and ADR-5 (timeout).

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully (tsc) with zero errors.
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors.
ESLint reports zero errors on all new/modified files.

scaffold(rootDir, child) on a fresh target creates the folder, writes a Zod-valid bober.config.json (from buildChildConfig), runs `git init`, and returns ScaffoldResult{folder, absPath, configWritten:true, gitInitialized:true}.
scaffold() into a pre-existing NON-EMPTY folder returns a ScaffoldResult with `error` set and leaves the folder's existing contents untouched (no overwrite, no delete, no spawn).
scaffold() never throws; mkdir/write/git-init failures are captured in ScaffoldResult.error (git init invoked via execa with reject:false).

run(spec) spawns process.execPath with the resolved dist/cli/index.js entry and ['run', task] in spec.cwd via execa({reject:false, timeout}), and returns ChildSpawnResult{cwd, exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut?, spawnError?} without throwing.
A default per-child timeout is applied when spec.timeoutMs is unset, and an exceeded timeout yields a result with timedOut true rather than hanging (ADR-5).

The child CLI entry is resolved to the parent's own dist/cli/index.js via fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) (not a bare PATH lookup), and a `--version` probe helper exists to verify the binary before fan-out (ADR-4).
All existing tests continue to pass with zero failures.

nonGoals: No mapBounded fan-out or per-child thunk orchestration (Sprint 3)
No outcome aggregation or RunState reading (Sprint 3)
No CLI command registration, runFleet, report writing, or credential fail-fast (Sprint 4)
Do not modify the `run` command or runPipeline
stopConditions: All ten success criteria pass programmatic or manual verification
scaffold + run can, against the real built dist/cli/index.js or a lightweight stub, produce a ChildSpawnResult, and the non-empty-folder safety case is proven by test
value.definitionOfDone: src/fleet/scaffolder.ts exports ChildScaffolder with scaffold(rootDir, child): Promise<ScaffoldResult> (reusing buildChildConfig from Sprint 1) and src/fleet/runner.ts exports ChildRunner with run(spec): Promise<ChildSpawnResult> plus a CLI-entry resolver and a --version probe helper. Errors are captured as data, never thrown. Collocated tests use temp dirs and cover fresh scaffold, non-empty-folder skip/safety, error capture, spawn result capture, default + exceeded timeout. Build, typecheck, lint clean; all tests pass.
assumptions: execa is the established subprocess primitive; the reject:false non-throwing pattern at src/utils/git.ts is the template, and execa supports a `timeout` option (used at src/providers/factory.ts).
The parent runs from a built dist/; resolving the parent's own dist/cli/index.js via import.meta.url is correct (ADR-4). Running from un-built source is unsupported.
git is available on PATH; a git-init failure is captured as ScaffoldResult.error, not thrown.
A folder is considered non-empty if it contains any entries (e.g. readdir length > 0).
outOfScope: Concurrency, isolation thunk, aggregation, report, CLI (later sprints)
value.generatorNotes:
READ FIRST: src/utils/git.ts (execa import + the {reject:false} pattern + any async fs helpers), src/providers/factory.ts (execa timeout usage), src/cli/index.ts (how it resolves its own entry via fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) and registers commands), and Sprint 1's manifest.ts/child-config.ts.

scaffolder.ts:
- scaffold(rootDir, child): resolve absPath = path.resolve(rootDir, child.folder). Check existence + emptiness with node:fs/promises (stat/readdir). If it exists and is non-empty → return { folder, absPath, configWritten:false, gitInitialized:false, error: 'folder exists and is non-empty' } WITHOUT touching it. Otherwise mkdir({recursive:true}), write bober.config.json (JSON.stringify(buildChildConfig(child), null, 2)) via writeFile, then `git init` via execa(..., { cwd: absPath, reject:false }). Capture any failure into error. NEVER throw.
- Use async fs only. No fs.*Sync.

runner.ts:
- resolveCliEntry(): const here = fileURLToPath(import.meta.url); resolve up to the package's dist/cli/index.js (compute relative to the module location, mirroring src/cli/index.ts entry handling). Export it so Sprint 4 can probe it.
- probeCliVersion(cliEntry): execa(process.execPath, [cliEntry, '--version'], { reject:false, timeout: 5000 }) → boolean ok.
- run(spec): const DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10*60*1000; execa(process.execPath, [resolveCliEntry(), 'run', spec.task], { cwd: spec.cwd, reject:false, timeout: spec.timeoutMs ?? DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_MS, maxBuffer: <bounded> }). Map execa result fields to ChildSpawnResult (exitCode, stdout, stderr, timedOut, and on spawn error set spawnError). NEVER throw.

Testing: for run(), prefer a tiny stub script invoked via process.execPath (e.g. a fixture .js that exits with a chosen code / sleeps to trigger timeout) so tests don't need the full pipeline. Use temp dirs (mkdtemp) and clean up; do not mock fs.

ESM .js import extensions; import type for types; no `any`.

sc-2-6: Force a failure (e.g. unwritable path) and confirm error is captured, not thrown.

sc-2-9: Read resolveCliEntry — confirm it uses fileURLToPath(import.meta.url) and resolves to dist/cli/index.js, NOT a bare 'agent-bober' PATH lookup; confirm a --version probe helper exists.
sc-2-10: full suite green.
Check: async fs only, .js import extensions, no leaked SDK types.

value.title: Bounded fan-out coordinator and outcome aggregator
value.description: Implement FleetCoordinator.execute() that fans children through the existing mapBounded() at the configured cap using a never-reject per-child thunk (scaffold → run, all errors captured as data), and OutcomeAggregator.aggregate() that resolves each child's status disk-primary from its newest .bober/runs/<runId>/state.json with an exit-code fallback. This is the critical isolation + concurrency sprint.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully (tsc) with zero errors.
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors.
ESLint reports zero errors on all new/modified files.

execute(manifest) drives children exclusively through mapBounded(children, manifest.concurrency, thunk) from src/orchestrator/workflow/scheduler.ts (no hand-rolled pool, no pre-spawn for-loop) and returns ChildExecution[] aligned to input order.
Peak concurrent in-flight children never exceeds the configured cap — verified by an instrumented thunk that tracks live count and asserts observed peak <= cap.

When one child's scaffold or run throws or rejects, every sibling still resolves to a ChildExecution and the batch is NOT aborted (the per-child thunk always resolves; errors captured as data). Verified by a sibling-survival test.

aggregate(execution) reads the child's RunState files; when one or more exist it returns ChildOutcome with status from the newest-by-startedAt RunState and source 'disk' (including the discovered runId).

When no RunState exists, aggregate() falls back to exitCode === 0 ? 'completed' : 'failed' with source 'exit-code'; when scaffold failed and no spawn occurred it returns 'failed'/'exit-code'. aggregate() never throws.
All existing tests continue to pass with zero failures.

nonGoals: No report building/writing, runFleet entrypoint, or CLI command (Sprint 4)
Do not modify mapBounded/Semaphore, runPipeline, or the `run` command
stopConditions: All nine success criteria pass programmatic or manual verification
The sibling-survival test and the peak-concurrency-<=-cap test both pass deterministically
value.definitionOfDone: src/fleet/coordinator.ts exports FleetCoordinator with execute(manifest): Promise<ChildExecution[]> wrapping mapBounded with a per-child thunk that try/catches scaffold+run and ALWAYS resolves to a ChildExecution{folder, scaffold, spawn?}. src/fleet/aggregator.ts exports OutcomeAggregator with aggregate(execution): Promise<ChildOutcome> using readRunStatesFromDisk (newest by startedAt) with exit-code fallback. Collocated tests cover mapBounded usage, peak<=cap, sibling-survival, disk-primary status, exit-code fallback, and scaffold-failed cases. Build/typecheck/lint clean; all tests pass.
assumptions: mapBounded(items, cap, fn) in src/orchestrator/workflow/scheduler.ts wraps a single shared Semaphore and resolves via Promise.all — therefore the per-child thunk MUST NEVER reject (errors as data), or one rejection aborts the batch. This is the load-bearing isolation invariant.

readRunStatesFromDisk (src/state/run-state.ts) returns RunState entries for a given project root and already swallows IO/JSON errors, returning empty when none exist; RunState carries a startedAt usable for newest-selection.
Children write to their own isolated cwd/.bober/runs/; the parent reads strictly post-exit, so there is no reader/writer race.
value.generatorNotes:
READ FIRST: src/orchestrator/workflow/scheduler.ts (EXACT mapBounded signature + Semaphore behavior + the Promise.all at the rejection-sensitive line; confirm how a thrown thunk propagates), src/state/run-state.ts (readRunStatesFromDisk signature + RunState shape + startedAt field; how run dirs are enumerated), src/mcp/run-manager.ts (RunState.status enum values), and Sprint 2's scaffolder.ts/runner.ts.

coordinator.ts:
- execute(manifest): build perChildThunk = (child) => async () => { try { const scaffold = await scaffolder.scaffold(manifest.rootDir, child); if (scaffold.error) return { folder: child.folder, scaffold, spawn: undefined }; const spawn = await runner.run({ cwd: scaffold.absPath, task: child.task, timeoutMs: <from child.config?> }); return { folder: child.folder, scaffold, spawn }; } catch (e) { return { folder: child.folder, scaffold: { folder: child.folder, absPath: '', configWritten:false, gitInitialized:false, error: String(e) }, spawn: undefined }; } }. CRITICAL: the thunk body is fully wrapped so it can NEVER reject. Then return mapBounded(manifest.children, manifest.concurrency, (child) => perChildThunk(child)()). Match mapBounded's actual (items, cap, fn) calling convention from scheduler.ts.
- Allow dependency injection of scaffolder + runner (constructor params or factory) so tests can substitute fakes that throw / track concurrency.

aggregator.ts:
- aggregate(execution): if execution.scaffold.error and no spawn → return { folder, status:'failed', source:'exit-code', exitCode: execution.spawn?.exitCode ?? -1 }. Else read RunStates: const states = await readRunStatesFromDisk(execution.scaffold.absPath); if states.length: pick newest by startedAt (string ISO compare desc), map RunState.status to ChildOutcome.status ('completed'|'failed'|'other' — map the RunState enum: completed→completed, failed/aborted→failed, running/other→other) and return source:'disk' with runId + runState. Else fallback to exitCode===0?'completed':'failed', source:'exit-code'. NEVER throw (readRunStatesFromDisk already swallows IO errors; guard anyway).

Testing: inject fake scaffolder/runner. For peak<=cap: the fake runner increments a shared counter on entry, records max, decrements on exit, with a small await tick to force overlap; assert max <= cap with cap < children.length. For sibling-survival: make one fake throw; assert all others present. For aggregator: create temp .bober/runs/<id>/state.json fixtures via run-state helpers (or write the files directly) and assert disk-primary selection + fallback.

ESM .js imports; import type; no `any`.
value.evaluatorNotes:
sc-3-4: Confirm execute() calls mapBounded with (children, concurrency, fn) and does NOT spawn in a plain for/Promise.all-of-all loop. Confirm input-order alignment.
sc-3-5: Run the instrumented peak-concurrency test with e.g. 6 children, cap 2; assert observed peak is exactly <= cap and that more than `cap` children DID run (not serialized by accident). Make it deterministic (counter + max), not timing-flaky.
sc-3-6: This is the most important check. Force one child's thunk path to throw (scaffold or run) and assert execute() still resolves with a ChildExecution for EVERY child and never rejects. Inspect the thunk to confirm the try/catch wraps everything.
sc-3-7/sc-3-8: With RunState fixtures, confirm newest-by-startedAt selection and the enum→status mapping; remove the state files and confirm exit-code fallback with source 'exit-code'; confirm scaffold-error path → failed; confirm aggregate never throws on a missing/garbage run dir.
sc-3-9: full suite green.

value.title: Portfolio reporter, runFleet entrypoint, and fleet CLI command
value.description: Implement PortfolioReporter (build + atomic write of .bober/fleet-report.json), the runFleet() entrypoint that orchestrates load → fail-fast credential check → execute → aggregate → report, and registerFleetCommand(program) that registers `agent-bober fleet <manifest.json>`. This sprint makes the feature user-visible end-to-end while leaving the `run` command and runPipeline untouched.

successCriteria.description: The project builds successfully (tsc) with zero errors.
TypeScript compilation produces zero type errors.
ESLint reports zero errors on all new/modified files.
PortfolioReporter.build(outcomes) returns a PortfolioReport with correct total/completed/failed/other counts (other = running/aborted/unknown) and an ISO-8601 generatedAt.
PortfolioReporter.write(rootDir, report) writes .bober/fleet-report.json atomically (temp file + rename) and returns the absolute path; partial/corrupt files are not left on failure.
runFleet(manifestPath, options) loads the manifest, runs execute → aggregate → build → write end-to-end and returns the PortfolioReport; --concurrency/--rootDir options override manifest fields.
When the manifest targets DeepSeek and neither DEEPSEEK_API_KEY nor a child providerConfig.apiKey is available, runFleet fails fast (throws/aborts) BEFORE spawning any child.

registerFleetCommand(program) registers a `fleet` command (positional manifest path + --concurrency/--rootDir options) following the existing command-registration pattern, and is wired into the CLI; running it returns exit code 0 even when some children fail.
The existing `run` command and runPipeline are unchanged (no diff to their signatures/behavior), confirmed by existing run-command tests still passing.
All existing tests continue to pass with zero failures.

nonGoals: Do not modify runPipeline, runRunCommand, or the `run` command contract
stopConditions: All ten success criteria pass programmatic or manual verification
An end-to-end run of `agent-bober fleet <manifest>` over a small manifest (e.g. against stub children) produces .bober/fleet-report.json with correct counts and exits 0
value.definitionOfDone: src/fleet/reporter.ts exports PortfolioReporter (build + atomic write). src/fleet/index.ts exports runFleet(manifestPath, options): Promise<PortfolioReport> (load → credential fail-fast → coordinator.execute → aggregate each → reporter.build → reporter.write) and registerFleetCommand(program). The CLI entry (src/cli/index.ts) calls registerFleetCommand. runFleet returns a report and the command exits 0 regardless of per-child failures. Collocated tests cover build counts, atomic write, end-to-end runFleet (with injected/stub children), and the credential fail-fast. Build/typecheck/lint clean; all tests pass and the `run` command tests are untouched and green.
assumptions: Atomic write mirrors the temp-file + rename approach used by writeRunState in src/state/run-state.ts.
CLI command registration follows the registerWorktreeCommand pattern in src/cli/index.ts (commander).

runFleet always resolves with a PortfolioReport for per-child failures and only throws on batch-setup failures (bad manifest, missing credentials, report-write failure) — resolved clarification Q2-failure-exit (exit 0).

Credential check: if any child's effective config uses the DeepSeek/openai-compat provider, require process.env.DEEPSEEK_API_KEY OR a providerConfig.apiKey on that child's config; otherwise fail fast.
outOfScope: Changing runPipeline or the run command
value.generatorNotes:
READ FIRST: src/state/run-state.ts (writeRunState atomic temp+rename pattern + where .bober paths come from), src/cli/index.ts (registerWorktreeCommand pattern, how commands are added, how the entry calls register* fns, and how options are parsed), src/cli/commands/run.ts (to mirror option handling WITHOUT modifying it), src/providers/factory.ts (DeepSeek key validation: DEEPSEEK_API_KEY / providerConfig.apiKey), and Sprints 1-3 modules.

reporter.ts:
- build(outcomes): tally total/completed/failed/other (other = anything not completed/failed), generatedAt = new Date().toISOString(). Return PortfolioReport.
- write(rootDir, report): write to <rootDir>/.bober/fleet-report.json via temp file + rename (copy the writeRunState technique; ensure .bober exists). Return abs path. This is the ONE place allowed to throw on IO failure.

index.ts (src/fleet/index.ts):
- runFleet(manifestPath, options): const manifest = await load(manifestPath); apply options.concurrency/rootDir overrides; CREDENTIAL FAIL-FAST: for each child compute effective config (buildChildConfig) and if it uses DeepSeek/openai-compat, ensure DEEPSEEK_API_KEY or providerConfig.apiKey present — else throw a clear error BEFORE any spawn; optionally probe the CLI entry (probeCliVersion from Sprint 2) and throw if missing (ADR-4). const executions = await coordinator.execute(manifest); const outcomes = await Promise.all(executions.map(e => aggregator.aggregate(e))); const report = reporter.build(outcomes); await reporter.write(manifest.rootDir, report); return report.
- registerFleetCommand(program): program.command('fleet <manifest>').option('--concurrency <n>', ...).option('--root <dir>', ...).action(async (manifest, opts) => { try { const report = await runFleet(manifest, { concurrency: opts.concurrency?Number(opts.concurrency):undefined, rootDir: opts.root }); print a summary (mirror run.ts summary style); process.exitCode = 0; } catch (e) { logger.error(...); process.exitCode = 1; } }). Per-child failures never set a non-zero code; only batch-setup errors do.
- Wire registerFleetCommand into src/cli/index.ts next to the other register*Command calls. Do NOT touch the run command.

Testing: inject fakes for coordinator/aggregator (or use stub children from Sprint 2 fixtures) to drive runFleet end-to-end deterministically. Test the credential fail-fast by unsetting DEEPSEEK_API_KEY and using a DeepSeek manifest with no providerConfig.apiKey → expect throw before any spawn. Test atomic write leaves no temp file on success and a valid JSON report. Use temp dirs; clean up.

ESM .js imports; import type; no `any`; async fs only.
value.evaluatorNotes:
sc-4-4/sc-4-5: Verify count tallies for a mixed outcomes list; verify the report file is valid JSON at .bober/fleet-report.json and that the write is atomic (no leftover temp file; a write to an unwritable dir throws).
sc-4-6: Drive runFleet with stub/injected children; confirm it returns a report and that --concurrency/--rootDir overrides take effect.
sc-4-7: CRITICAL — with DEEPSEEK_API_KEY unset and a DeepSeek manifest lacking providerConfig.apiKey, confirm runFleet throws BEFORE any child spawn (assert no folders scaffolded / no spawn). With the key set, confirm it proceeds.
sc-4-8: Inspect registerFleetCommand — confirm it matches the commander registration pattern and is actually wired into src/cli/index.ts; confirm the action sets exit 0 on per-child failures and only non-zero on setup errors.
sc-4-9: Diff-check that run.ts / runPipeline are unchanged; run their existing tests.
sc-4-10: full suite green.
Also verify: atomic-write reuse, async fs only, .js extensions, no SDK leakage, no `any`.
